S14.01.note: The + button's visible icon-only label is the MENU_LABEL constant; the file chooser itself is the OS dialog.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Click the + button labelled More composer options next to the message box.
Click Add photos & files and choose a file in the device file chooser.
Look for the file chip above the message box; then send a short message and check the file is listed on your message.
S14.01.where: More composer options (+ button in the message box) > Add photos & files

S14.02.needs: a file to drag from Finder
steps: Open a chat and keep it visible.
Drag a file from Finder over the chat area.
Wait for the overlay to appear with the words Drop files here, then release the file.
Check that a file chip appears above the message box and that it is sent with the next message.
S14.02.where: Drag a file from Finder onto the chat window (overlay reads Drop files here)

S14.03.note: The paste handler is in code with no visible text of its own, so no label is given.
steps: Copy an image (for example a screenshot) to the clipboard.
Click in the message box of a chat.
Press Command+V.
Check that an image thumbnail appears above the message box and that it is sent with the next message.
S14.03.where: Message box in the chat composer, then Command+V after copying an image

S14.05.note: No separate photo-library picker was found in code; the photo route is the same file chooser that the Mac shows.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files.
In the file chooser, pick two or more photos (use Command+click) and confirm.
Check that every photo appears as a thumbnail above the message box.
S14.05.where: More composer options > Add photos & files

S14.06.needs: the Electron desktop app and Screen Recording permission for the app on macOS
S14.06.note: The composer's own More composer options menu did not show a screenshot row in code; the capture is the File menu item. The Capture screen button in the feedback dialog is for feedback, not chat attachments.
steps: In the Electron desktop app, open the File menu.
Click Screenshot to Chat, or press the screenshot shortcut.
Wait for the capture to finish, then look at the chat composer for a new image thumbnail.
Send the message and check the screenshot is attached to it.
S14.06.where: Desktop menu File > Screenshot to Chat (or its keyboard shortcut)

S14.07.needs: the Electron desktop app, Screen Recording permission, and a second app window in front
S14.07.note: Code captures the window in front of the app, not a window the user picks from a list. No picker was found.
steps: Open another app window and bring it to the front, with the desktop app behind it.
Press the Window to Chat shortcut.
Wait for the notice and then look for a new image thumbnail in the chat composer.
Send the message and check the window capture is attached.
S14.07.where: Keyboard shortcut Window to Chat (no menu item)

S14.10.needs: a file already in the Library
steps: Make sure the Library holds at least one file (Library in the sidebar).
Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add from library and choose a file from the list.
Check that the file chip appears above the message box and is sent with the next message.
S14.10.where: More composer options > Add from library

S14.11.needs: a connected code account with at least one repository (not checked)
S14.11.note: The sidebar entry that opens the Code page was not found in app-nav-items.ts, so the path to the Code page is unverified.
steps: Open the Code page of the app.
Click the Select repository chip.
Pick a repository from the list that opens.
Check that the chosen repository is shown as the context for the task.
S14.11.where: Code page > Select repository (repository chip in the code composer)

steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files.
In the file chooser select several files at once and confirm.
Check that all of them appear as chips or thumbnails above the message box.
S14.15.where: More composer options > Add photos & files

steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose an image file.
Look above the message box for a small square thumbnail of the image.
S14.16.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose an image)

S14.17.needs: a PDF, a spreadsheet and a code file
S14.17.note: The kind names PDF, Spreadsheet, Code, Document, Text, Presentation and File are in AttachmentPreview.tsx; the icon glyphs were not checked on screen.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a PDF, a spreadsheet and a code file.
Compare the icon on each chip with the file type.
S14.17.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a PDF, spreadsheet, code or other file)

steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose any file.
Look at the chip above the message box for the file name and its size (for example KB or MB).
S14.18.where: More composer options > Add photos & files

S14.19.needs: a large file, and a slow connection helps the status stay visible
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a large file.
Watch the chip: it should show Preparing, Uploading or Verifying text under the file name while the upload runs.
S14.19.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a large file)

S14.21.note: The button that opens project settings was not confirmed; the Projects page mounts the settings dialog, and a failed status shows Not indexed or Keyword search only, with a retry control, not a separate Failed word.
steps: Open Projects in the sidebar and open a project.
Open the project's settings and find the Files section.
Upload a file with the Upload button.
Watch the status next to the file: Indexing for search while it runs, then Keyword search only or Not indexed when it finishes.
S14.21.where: Projects > open a project > project settings > Files (Indexing for search status on each file)

S14.22.note: Code hides the progress line when a chip is ready, and no Ready word is shown; the tester can only see the absence of progress text.
steps: Attach a file with Add photos & files.
Wait until the chip stops showing Uploading or Preparing text.
Check that the Send button is enabled and sends the message with the file.
S14.22.where: Composer chip after a file finishes uploading

labels.text: was read because it is too long to read in full.

S14.23.note: The notice comes from a response header after sending, so it appears after the send, not in the composer.
steps: Attach a long text or PDF file with Add photos & files.
Send the message.
Look under your own message bubble for the notice that starts with Only part of.
Compare with Expected: the notice names the file.
S14.23.where: Under your sent message (notice reads Only part of NAME was read because it is too long to read in full.)

S14.24.needs: a file the chat cannot read (for example an unusual binary type)
S14.24.note: The chooser may block some types through the accept attribute, so the tester may need to force a type that the chooser still allows.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a file of an unsupported type.
Look for the notice that names the file and says it has an unsupported file type.
S14.24.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a file type the chat cannot read)

labels.text: is password protected. Remove the password and upload it again.

S14.25.note: The notice is produced on the server when the message is sent; where it appears on screen was not traced.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and choose a PDF that has a password.
Send the message and read the reply area.
Check for the notice that says the file is password protected and to remove the password and upload it again.
S14.25.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose a password-protected PDF), then send

S14.26.needs: a way to make an upload fail (for example turning Wi-Fi off)
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options, then Add photos & files and choose a file.
Make the upload fail, for example by turning Wi-Fi off straight after choosing the file.
Look at the chip for Upload failed and a Retry button under the file name.
Turn Wi-Fi back on, click Retry, and check the upload runs again.
S14.26.where: Attachment chip under the message box (Retry on a failed upload)

S14.27.needs: a large file so the upload lasts long enough to cancel
S14.27.note: The X button's accessible name is Cancel upload of NAME while uploading; its visible glyph is an X icon.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options, then Add photos & files and choose a large file.
While the chip shows Uploading, click the X button on that chip.
Check that the upload stops and the chip is removed.
Send a message and check the cancelled file is not sent.
S14.27.where: Attachment chip under the message box, the X button while Uploading shows

steps: Attach two or more files with Add photos & files.
Click the X button on one chip.
Check that only that chip disappears.
Send the message and check the removed file is not in the sent message.
S14.28.where: Attachment chip under the message box, the X button (Remove NAME)

steps: Attach a file with Add photos & files.
Attach the same file again with Add photos & files.
Look for the notice that says the file is already attached.
Check the file is listed only once when you send.
S14.31.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose the same file twice)

S14.32.needs: a file that fails (for example an image larger than the image limit)
steps: Attach a file that will fail, for example an image over the image size limit or a file that cannot be uploaded.
Look at the failed chip for the error text under its file name.
Hover the error text to see its full reason in the tooltip.
Check that the error names that file, not a general message.
S14.32.where: Attachment chip under the message box (error text under the failed file)

S14.33.needs: several files, including one that will be refused
S14.33.note: The notice reads Attached N of M files. Not attached: ... or None of the M files were attached: ...
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Click Add photos & files and select several files, including one that will be refused (for example a duplicate or an unsupported file).
Read the single notice that follows.
Check that it says how many files were attached and lists the refused files.
S14.33.where: More composer options > Add photos & files (choose several files, with one that is refused)

labels.text: Saved to your Library until you delete them.

S14.34.note: The retention text is a hover tooltip on the row, not visible text in the menu; the number of days comes from RESOURCE_RECOVERY_WINDOW_DAYS.
steps: Click the + button labelled More composer options.
Hover the mouse over the Add photos & files row and wait for the tooltip.
Read the tooltip for whether files are kept and for how long.
Open a temporary chat and repeat, then compare with the text that says files are deleted with the temporary chat.
S14.34.where: More composer options > hover Add photos & files (tooltip)

S14.35.needs: a Free account or a paid account, a file to upload (PDF for document, PNG or JPG for image), a model that cannot read that file type
S14.35.note: The warning is shown only when the selected model cannot read the file, and it is a warning with a fix button, not a block before sending. The attach menu and model picker labels were not found by search, so the tester must find them on screen. The free-plan variant of this warning uses "Use Free Auto" instead of "Use Auto".
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Attach a PDF or other document with the attach control in the composer (the menu label was not verified in code).
Select a model that cannot read documents or images (the model picker location was not verified in code).
Look above the text box for the warning that starts "The selected model can't read the attached document." (or "image" for pictures).
Check that the "Use Auto" button is present and that clicking "Choose a compatible model" lists models that can read the file, compared with Expected.
S14.35.where: New chat screen > attach a document or image with the attach control in the composer > choose a model that cannot read that file type from the model picker > the alert appears above the text box, with the buttons "Use Auto", "Remove attachments" and "Choose a compatible model"

labels.text: Local models on this device cannot read attachments. Switch to a cloud model or remove the attachment.

S14.36.needs: a local model available on the device (desktop app), a file to upload
S14.36.note: The local-model alert was located in code, but how a person selects a local model was not verified; the free-plan alert ("This free model accepts text only..." with "Use Free Auto") is a related alternative path that appears for restricted free models. The "Switch to a cloud model" text appears twice in ChatComposerNew.tsx, once for a local-model project conflict and once for the local-attachment conflict.
steps: Sign in and open a new chat.
Select a local model that runs on this device (the picker location was not verified in code).
Attach any file with the attach control in the composer.
Look for the alert that says "Local models on this device cannot read attachments." with the text "Switch to a cloud model or remove the attachment."
Compare with Expected: the alert names the alternative (switch to a cloud model) and the removal option, and the message is not sent through the local model.
S14.36.where: New chat screen > select a local model (on-device) from the model picker > attach a file in the composer > the alert appears above the text box with "Switch to a cloud model" and "Remove attachment"
